summary: The per-atom element array handed to the Python model is built with the descriptor count as its length instead of the atom count, so the model receives the wrong number of element types (and reads past the end of ielems when ndescriptors > natomneigh).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx:142-150: 'n_d = data.ndescriptors / n_a = data.nlistatoms / ... elem_cp = create_array(dev, data.ielems, (n_d,), True) / en_cp = create_array(dev, data.eatoms, (n_a,), False) / beta_cp = create_array(dev, data.betas, (n_a, n_d), False)'.  The CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_model_python_couple.pyx:112 uses the atom count: 'elem_np = np.asarray(<int[:n_a]> &data.ielems[0])'.  ielems is allocated per atom, not per descriptor: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:212 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_ielems, ielems, natomneigh_max, "mliap_data:ielems")'.  The model contract is per-atom: python/lammps/mliap/pytorch.py:107-114 'def forward(self, elems, descriptors, beta, energy, use_gpu_data=False): ... elems : numpy.array  Per atom element types', and python/lammps/mliap/pytorch.py:264 uses 'elems.shape[0]' as the atom count.
failure_scenario: pair_style mliap model mliappy ... with a multi-element torch model (UnpackElems/ElemwiseModels): elems has length ndescriptors instead of nlistatoms, so 'torch.zeros(elems.shape[0], ...)' builds a tensor with the wrong first dimension and either raises a shape error or silently produces wrong energies/betas. With a system whose atom count is smaller than ndescriptors (e.g. a 2-atom test cell with a 55-component SNAP descriptor) create_array reads 55 ints from a 2-int device buffer -> out-of-bounds read. The shipped kokkos example (examples/mliap/mliap_pytorch_Ta06A_kokkos.py, single element, IgnoreElems) discards elems and therefore does not expose this.
suggested_fix: Change the shape to (n_a,): 'elem_cp = create_array(dev, data.ielems, (n_a,), True)'.

summary: The total energy is reduced with cupy.sum() unconditionally, so on the non-CUDA (dev == 0) path -- where the arrays are numpy and cupy may not even be importable -- compute_gradients raises NameError on every step.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx:13-16 makes cupy optional ('try: import cupy / except ImportError: pass'), and create_array() only uses cupy when 'device == 1' (line 116), returning numpy arrays otherwise (lines 123-133).  Line 159 then does 'energy = cupy.sum(en_cp)' for both paths.  The CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_model_python_couple.pyx:119 uses 'energy = np.sum(en_np)'.  The dev flag is compile-time CUDA-only (src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.h:145-149 '#if defined(KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA) dev(1) #else dev(0)') and cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:281-292 builds this .pyx for every Kokkos backend, so the dev == 0 path is a supported configuration.
failure_scenario: Kokkos Serial/OpenMP build with MLIAP_ENABLE_PYTHON and no cupy installed: every call of MLIAPPYKokkos_compute_gradients raises NameError: name 'cupy' is not defined; MLIAPModelPythonKokkos::compute_gradients (src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:146-151) sees PyErr_Occurred and aborts the run with 'Running python model failure.'
suggested_fix: Use 'energy = cupy.sum(en_cp) if dev == 1 else numpy.sum(en_cp)' (or reduce inside create_array's owner module) so the host path does not require cupy.

summary: The numneighs property builds a float64 array over the int32 neighbor-count buffer (is_int passed as False), returning garbage counts and reading twice as many bytes as the array holds.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:374-378: 'def numneighs(self): ... return create_array(self.data.dev, self.data.numneighs, [self.natomneigh],False)' -- the last argument is create_array's is_int flag (lines 123-144: False selects cupy.double / '<double[:shape[0]]>').  Every other integer array passes True (iatoms:384, ielems:390, pair_i:400, jatoms:410, jelems:416, elems:360).  numneighs is an int array: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.h:185 'int *numneighs;' and src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:215 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_numneighs, numneighs, natomneigh_max, "mliap_data:numneighs")'.  The CPU original agrees: src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:244 'return np.asarray(<int[:self.natomneigh]> &self.data.numneighs[0])'.
failure_scenario: Any unified model (mliap model unified ... with pair_style mliap/kk) that segments its per-pair arrays with 'data.numneighs' gets natomneigh float64 values reinterpreted from pairs of int32 counts (e.g. counts 12,14 -> 5.9e-322) and reads natomneigh*8 bytes out of a natomneigh*4-byte allocation, i.e. wrong per-atom neighbor counts plus an out-of-bounds read. The in-tree LJ/JAX examples only use rij/pair_i, so nothing in the test suite catches it.
suggested_fix: Pass True as the is_int argument: 'create_array(self.data.dev, self.data.numneighs, [self.natomneigh], True)'.

summary: Reference counting for unified_interface is only balanced by accident: mliap_unified_connect_kokkos returns a NEW reference that build_unified never releases, and the extra Py_DECREF in ~MLIAPDummyModelKokkos (on top of its base class's) happens to cancel it -- so this is NOT the double release it looks like, but removing either half alone breaks it.
evidence: Cythonizing src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:492-549 ('cdef public object mliap_unified_connect_kokkos') produces '__Pyx_INCREF((PyObject *)__pyx_v_unified_int); __pyx_r = ((PyObject *)__pyx_v_unified_int); ... __Pyx_XGIVEREF(__pyx_r);' -- an owned reference is handed to the caller.  src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:243-255 then adds two more: 'PyObject *unified_interface = mliap_unified_connect_kokkos(...); // Borrowed references must be manually incremented / model->unified_interface = unified_interface; Py_INCREF(...); descriptor->unified_interface = unified_interface; Py_INCREF(...);' and never DECREFs the returned one -> 3 owned references.  Releases: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:144 'Py_DECREF(unified_interface)' plus its base src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:126 (MLIAPDummyModelKokkos derives from MLIAPDummyModel, mliap_unified_kokkos.h:38) plus src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:39 for the descriptor (the kokkos descriptor's copy is commented out at mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:44) = 3.  The CPU version takes the same 3 references but releases only 2, i.e. it leaks one.
failure_scenario: No crash today: 3 increfs vs 3 decrefs. The hazard is the asymmetry. Removing the duplicate Py_DECREF at line 144 on its own turns the kokkos path into the same one-reference leak the CPU version already has; conversely, fixing that leak by adding the missing Py_DECREF for the value returned by mliap_unified_connect_kokkos() while line 144 stays gives 3 increfs vs 4 decrefs, so the MLIAPUnifiedInterfaceKokkos is freed while the Python-side 'unified.interface' attribute still points at it -> use-after-free at the next garbage collection.
suggested_fix: Make the ownership explicit in both build_unified implementations: keep the two Py_INCREFs, add the missing 'Py_DECREF(unified_interface);' for the value returned by mliap_unified_connect*(), fix the misleading 'Borrowed references' comment, and then delete the duplicate Py_DECREF at mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:144 so each destructor releases exactly the reference its own class holds.

summary: torch is imported unconditionally at module scope and torch.cuda.nvtx is called on every compute, so the coupling module cannot be loaded without PyTorch and fails at run time with a CPU-only PyTorch build, neither of which is true of the CPU original.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx:12 'import torch' (unguarded, unlike the optional cupy import at 13-16) and lines 140/151/154/156 'torch.cuda.nvtx.range_push(...)/range_pop()'.  The CPU original imports torch lazily and only for torch checkpoints: src/ML-IAP/mliap_model_python_couple.pyx:65-67 'if str_fname.endswith(".pt") ... import torch'.  torch.cuda.nvtx dispatches to a stub that raises RuntimeError('NVTX functions not installed. Are you sure you have a CUDA build?') when torch was built without CUDA.
failure_scenario: A user with a pickled numpy model (no torch) or a CPU-only torch wheel builds LAMMPS with KOKKOS+MLIAP_ENABLE_PYTHON: PyImport_ImportModule("mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos") fails (ImportError) -> 'Loading MLIAPPYKokkos coupling module failure.', or the module loads and every compute_gradients raises RuntimeError from range_push.
suggested_fix: Guard the torch import like the cupy one and wrap the nvtx range_push/range_pop calls so they are only issued when a CUDA-capable torch is present (or drop them).

summary: The betas, descriptors, gradforce and graddesc setters cast raw device pointers to host Cython memoryviews and copy into them, which faults on a GPU build (as the accompanying print statements half-admit).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:279-285 'cdef double[:, :] betas_view = <double[:self.nlistatoms, :self.ndescriptors]> &self.data.betas[0] ... print("This code has not been tested or optimized for the GPU ...")', likewise descriptors:291, gradforce:273 and graddesc:439.  Unlike every getter, these do not go through create_array()/cupy even when self.data.dev == 1.  The pointers are device pointers: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.h:115-116 'betas(base.k_betas.view_device().data()), descriptors(base.k_descriptors.view_device().data())' and :141 'graddesc(base.k_graddesc.view_device().data())'.
failure_scenario: A unified model on a CUDA build that assigns data.descriptors = ... (the documented way for compute_descriptors to return its result, as the CPU version at src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:153-159 supports) makes the CPU memcpy into device memory -> segmentation fault or silent corruption.
suggested_fix: Route the setters through a device-aware copy (cupy array assignment when dev == 1) instead of a host memoryview, or raise a clear error when dev == 1 rather than printing a note and writing anyway.

summary: forward_exchange/reverse_exchange wrap the actual exchange call in a try with a bare except, so a failure that happens after the C++ exchange started is retried through the second code path (exchange applied twice) and genuine type errors are masked.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:204-225 (and the identical reverse_exchange at 235-256): the try block contains both the pointer extraction AND 'self.data.forward_exchange(<float*>copy_from_ptr, ...)', which is declared 'except +' (line 87) so any C++ exception becomes a Python exception; the bare 'except:' at line 215 then re-runs the whole block using 'copy_from.data.ptr'.  The deliberate 'raise TypeError(f"Unsupported comms type: ...")' at line 214 is caught by the same bare except.  The fallback branch is commented '#Attempt assuming Numpy data' but uses the cupy attribute '.data.ptr'; a real numpy array has no such attribute.
failure_scenario: A model calls data.forward_exchange(torch_tensor_a, torch_tensor_b, 3) with dtype torch.int64: the try raises TypeError('Unsupported comms type'), the bare except swallows it, then 'copy_from.data.ptr' raises AttributeError on the tensor -- the user sees an unrelated AttributeError. If instead the C++ forward_comm throws mid-exchange, the except branch re-issues the same comm and ghost data is exchanged twice.
suggested_fix: Select the pointer-extraction path with hasattr/type checks (or a narrow 'except AttributeError'), and move the forward_exchange/reverse_exchange calls out of the try block so they are never retried.

summary: MLIAPDataKokkosDevice::numneighs is initialized from the host mirror pointer while every other array is initialized from the device view, so the Python side wraps host memory as if it were device memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.h:131 'numneighs(base.numneighs),' versus :132-140 'iatoms(base.k_iatoms.view_device().data()), pair_i(...view_device().data()), ielems(...), jatoms(...), jelems(...), elems(...), rij(...)'.  base.numneighs is the host mirror: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:215 'memoryKK->create_kokkos(k_numneighs, numneighs, natomneigh_max, ...)' with src/KOKKOS/memory_kokkos.h:38-43 'data = TYPE(name,n1); array = data.view_host().data();'.  The counts themselves are produced on the device (src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.cpp:247 'd_numneighs(ii) = count;' followed by 'modified(execution_space, NUMNEIGHS_MASK)').
failure_scenario: On a CUDA build (dev == 1) src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:378 hands this host address to cupy.cuda.UnownedMemory, so any kernel touching data.numneighs dereferences a host pointer as device memory (illegal access); with kokkos auto_sync disabled the values are also stale because only the device view was updated.
suggested_fix: Initialize it like the others, 'numneighs(base.k_numneighs.view_device().data())', so the exported pointer lives in the same memory space as the rest of the struct.

summary: MLIAPDataPy wraps a pointer to a stack-local MLIAPDataKokkosDevice built by the C++ caller, so a Python model that keeps the data object (deferred/asynchronous evaluation) dereferences dead stack memory -- unlike the CPU version, where the pointer is the long-lived MLIAPData.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:473-488 'pydata = MLIAPDataPy(); pydata.data = data; unified_int.compute_gradients(pydata)'.  The caller passes the address of a stack temporary: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:55-57 'MLIAPDataKokkosDevice raw_data(*kokkos_data); compute_descriptors_python_kokkos(unified_interface, &raw_data);' (same at :76 and :169, and src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_kokkos.cpp:144).  In the CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:338-341 the same assignment stores 'MLIAPData *data', the object owned by the pair style, which stays alive between calls.
failure_scenario: A unified model that stores 'self.data = data' in compute_descriptors and uses it later (e.g. from a torch autograd hook or in compute_forces of the same step) reads a MLIAPDataKokkosDevice that no longer exists -> garbage pointers/sizes and a crash or silent corruption.  In-tree models only use data within the call, so the examples do not expose it.
suggested_fix: Give MLIAPDataPy a copy of the MLIAPDataKokkosDevice struct (or null out pydata.data after the call returns) so a retained object fails loudly instead of reading freed stack memory.

summary: Dead local 'cdef void* ptr = data.ielems' and a duplicated cimport of uintptr_t.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx:145 'cdef void* ptr = data.ielems' is never used afterwards (lines 146-161 use data.ielems directly).  Lines 6 and 19 both contain 'from libc.stdint cimport uintptr_t'.  Neither appears in the CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_model_python_couple.pyx.
failure_scenario: No run-time effect; leftover debugging scaffolding that obscures the code.
suggested_fix: Delete line 145 and the duplicate cimport on line 19.

summary: The gradforce/betas/descriptors setters print an unconditional warning on every call from every MPI rank.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:276 'print("This code has not been tested or optimized for the GPU, if you are getting this warning optimize gradforce")', :285 '... optimize ' and :294 '... optimize descriptors'.  None of these exist in the CPU original (src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:137-159).  They are printed even when self.data.dev == 0, where the code path is the tested one.
failure_scenario: A unified model that sets descriptors every step floods stdout with one line per rank per timestep, which also breaks log-file comparisons in the regression tests.
suggested_fix: Drop the print statements or emit them once, and only when self.data.dev == 1.

summary: eatoms was silently changed from a write-only property to a read-only property, so unified models that assign per-atom energies as they do with the CPU version get an AttributeError; its NULL check still raises the setter's message.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:296-300: '@property / def eatoms(self): / if self.data.eatoms is NULL: raise ValueError("attempt to set NULL eatoms") / return create_array(...)'.  The CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:161-167 defines it as '@write_only_property def eatoms(self, value): ... eatoms_view[:] = value_view'.  A property with only fget raises AttributeError on assignment.
failure_scenario: An existing unified model doing 'data.eatoms = my_energies' runs under pair_style mliap but fails with AttributeError under mliap/kk; and reading a NULL eatoms reports 'attempt to set NULL eatoms' although nothing was being set.
suggested_fix: Keep the setter (device-aware) in addition to the getter, and fix the message to 'attempt to read NULL eatoms'.

summary: The extern block declares MLIAPDummyDescriptor::elements as 'char *' although the C++ member is 'char **'.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:94 'char *elements     # names of unique elements' versus src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.h (the class this extern block describes, included by mliap_unified_kokkos.h) and the CPU original src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:82 'char **elements'.  Harmless today only because the field is never accessed from Cython, so no C++ code is generated for it.
failure_scenario: The first .pyx change that reads or writes descriptor.elements generates 'char *' code against a 'char **' member and fails to compile, or (with a cast) corrupts the element-name table.
suggested_fix: Declare it as 'char **elements' to match mliap_unified.h.

summary: The gamma property references self.gama_nnz, a typo that makes the property raise AttributeError whenever gamma is non-NULL (inherited unchanged from the CPU original).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:329 'return create_array(self.data.dev, self.data.gamma, [self.nlistatoms, self.gama_nnz],False)'; the property defined at line 322 is named gamma_nnz, and the neighbouring gamma_row_index/gamma_col_index properties (lines 335, 341) spell it correctly.  The same typo is in src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified_couple.pyx:195.
failure_scenario: A model that reads data.gamma (once gradgrad support is wired up) gets AttributeError: 'MLIAPDataPy' object has no attribute 'gama_nnz' instead of the array.
suggested_fix: Spell it self.gamma_nnz (and fix the CPU original at the same time).

summary: MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos::set_elements() is unreachable: the Cython interface calls it through a MLIAPDummyDescriptor* and the method is not virtual, so the base version always runs (which also means the missing allocated_elements assignment cannot leak).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:492-493 declares 'mliap_unified_connect_kokkos(char *fname, MLIAPDummyModel * model, MLIAPDummyDescriptor * descriptor)' and line 543 calls 'unified_int.descriptor.set_elements(elements, nelements)'; the generated C++ is '__pyx_v_unified_int->descriptor->set_elements(__pyx_v_elements, __pyx_v_nelements);' with descriptor typed 'LAMMPS_NS::MLIAPDummyDescriptor *'.  set_elements is declared non-virtual in both src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.h:34 and src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.h:35, so src/ML-IAP/mliap_unified.cpp:108-114 runs (including 'allocated_elements = 1'), never src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:122-128.  build_unified passes a MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos* that is implicitly upcast at the call (mliap_unified_kokkos.cpp:243).
failure_scenario: No run-time effect (the base implementation is the correct one); the dead override is misleading and would silently start leaking the strdup'ed element names if set_elements were ever made virtual.
suggested_fix: Delete the MLIAPDummyDescriptorKokkos::set_elements override (and its declaration), or make set_elements virtual and add the missing 'allocated_elements = 1'.

summary: cupy.cuda.UnownedMemory is given the element count where it expects a size in bytes, understating the wrapped allocation by a factor of 4/8/24.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:124-128 'size=1 / for i in shape: size = size*i / ... mem = cupy.cuda.UnownedMemory(ptr=int(<uintptr_t> pointer), owner=None, size=size)' -- size is the number of elements, but UnownedMemory's size argument is documented as the size of the memory allocation in bytes.  The same code is duplicated in src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx:111-117.
failure_scenario: cupy does not currently validate the memptr size in ndarray.__init__, so this is latent; any cupy operation or future version that bounds-checks against MemoryPointer.mem.size sees an array 8x larger than its memory and either errors or refuses a legal view.
suggested_fix: Multiply by the item size, e.g. 'size = size * (4 if is_int else 8)', before constructing UnownedMemory.

summary: The dev flag that tells the Python side whether the exported pointers are device memory is set from KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA only, so a Kokkos HIP/SYCL GPU build reports dev == 0 and the .pyx wraps device pointers in host numpy arrays.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/mliap_data_kokkos.h:144-149 'pairmliap(...), #if defined(KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA) dev(1) #else dev(0) #endif' while all the exported pointers come from '...view_device().data()' (lines 113-141) regardless of backend. src/KOKKOS/mliap_unified_couple_kokkos.pyx:134-144 and src/KOKKOS/mliap_model_python_couple_kokkos.pyx:123-133 use the numpy/host branch whenever dev != 1 ('np.asarray(<double[:shape[0]]>pointer)'). Nothing in cmake/Modules/Packages/KOKKOS.cmake:255-293 restricts ML-IAP+python to the CUDA backend.
failure_scenario: Kokkos HIP build with MLIAP_ENABLE_PYTHON: data.rij / data.pair_i etc. return numpy arrays constructed over HIP device pointers, and the first read from Python segfaults.
suggested_fix: Set dev from any GPU backend ('#if defined(KOKKOS_ENABLE_CUDA) || defined(KOKKOS_ENABLE_HIP)') or make the ML-IAP python coupling error out at build/init time on unsupported GPU backends.
